govdocs-archive_org-nsia-FBILiuzzoViola_: Paul Magnusson’s Relatives of Rights Worker Liuzzo File $2 Million Claim covers the civil-rights case. Viola Liuzzo was murdered in 1965. The claim sought justice. The file belongs to the civil-rights archive. The item is a fragment of press history.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-JohnsonPriscill: Svetlana Alliluyeva’s Twenty Letters to a Friend — Excerpt, Part II — is a memoir passage. Alliluyeva was Stalin’s daughter. Her defection made headlines. The memoir was a bestseller. The file belongs to the literary archive. The item is a fragment of publishing history.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-KaiserRobertBla: Steven V. Roberts’s The Sirhan B. Sirhan Literary Negotiations, Etc., Inc. covers the RFK killer’s book deals. Publishers courted the assassin. The deals sparked outrage. The file belongs to the press archive. The item is a fragment of press history.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-MumfordPamelaLi: This FBI interview — Pamela Lillian Mumford on Albert Osborne, February — is a Bureau file. The declassified interview is a primary source. Osborne was the mysterious missionary. The interview may hold a clue. The file belongs to the government archive.
the-lives-of-the-twelve-caesars-volume-0: Suetonius gives us the old world's most ill-famed portrait of a mad king. Young Gaius Caligula ruled Rome for just four years, calling himself a living god, wasting the gold in the vaults, and striking fear into the Senate until knives ended him in 41 AD. Set down a lifetime later from court talk and state papers, the life is as gripping as it is shocking.
ideala: Sarah Grand — the firebrand of the New Woman movement — creates in Ideala a heroine who thinks for herself about marriage, morality, and women's rights. The novel challenged Victorian conventions and made its author famous. A bold, important voice from the dawn of modern feminism.
a-woman-s-life-work-labors-and-experienc: Laura Haviland of Michigan tells of her life-work — hiding runaways, teaching freed folk, and a long life of kind deeds. Her plain tale both shames and lifts the heart. The true story of a brave, good woman. Her courage helped bend a nation's conscience toward justice.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abila: This 1913 reference piece on Abila — the name of several ancient towns, in Syria and beyond. The entry sorts the sites with care. Lysanias of Abilene ruled one of them. Geography for students of the Gospels. Luke's Gospel names its tetrarch in passing.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-aelia-flaccil: A 1913 entry on Aelia Flaccilla — the pious wife of Theodosius the Great. Johann Peter Kirsch tells her story. She nursed the sick with her own hands. The Church honors her as a saint. An empress of charity. Her statue stood in the Hippodrome's honor.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alexander-agr: A 1913 entry on Alexander Agricola — the Franco-Flemish composer of the Burgundian court. James Völker notes his masses and chansons. His music crossed the Alps. The Renaissance sang his melodies. A prince of the polyphonists. His Missa Malheur me bat is famed.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-aquila-and-pr: A 1913 entry on Aquila and Priscilla — St. Paul's fellow tentmakers. Anthony Maas honors the devoted pair. Their house was a church. They risked their necks for Paul. The apostle's beloved helpers. Their feast crowns the summer's start. Their house church met in Ephesus.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-aquila: This 1913 reference article on Aquila — the proselyte who rendered the Old Testament into Greek. John Joseph A'Becket notes his literal version. The rabbis prized his exactness. The scholars consult his fragments. The translator of the second century. His version served the synagogue's need.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-arindela: A 1913 entry on Arindela — the Palestinian town, now a titular see. Its bishops grace the old lists. The entry preserves its modest record. The Church keeps its ancient name. A see of the Holy Land. Its site lies near the Dead Sea.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ascoli-satria: A 1913 entry on Ascoli Satriano and Cirignola — the united Apulian diocese. Ernesto Buonaiuti gives its story. Its bishops serve the Tavoliere plain. The entry traces the old sees. A diocese of the southern fields. Its churches dot the Apulian plain.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ave-maris-ste: A 1913 entry on Ave Maris Stella — Hail, Star of the Sea. Hugh Henry unfolds its ancient hymn. The sailors sang it on the waves. The Office keeps its stately verse. The hymn of the seafarers' Queen. Its plainsong is grave and sweet.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-avila: A 1913 entry on Avila — St. Teresa's walled city. Thomas Shahan honors its saintly glory. Her convents dot the granite town. The mystic's Spain begins here. The city of the great reform. Its walls are Spain's finest. Its mystics made the city famed.
